NEW YORK, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SELLAS Life Sciences Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: SLS) (“SELLAS” or the “Company”), a late-stage clinical biopharmaceutical company focused on the development of novel therapies for a broad range of cancer indications, today announced the pricing of its previously announced underwritten public offering of 11,538,462 shares of its common stock at a public offering price of $13.00 per share. All of the shares in the offering will be sold by SELLAS, with gross proceeds to SELLAS expected to be $150.0 million before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and offering expenses. In addition, SELLAS has also granted the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to 1,730,769 additional shares of its common stock at the public offering price, less underwriting discounts and commissions. The offering is expected to close on November 20, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions.

J.P. Morgan and TD Cowen are acting as the lead book-running managers for the offering. Mizuho is also acting as a book-running manager for the offering. A.G.P./Alliance Global Partners and Maxim Group LLC are acting as lead managers for the offering.

The public offering is being made pursuant to a shelf registration statement on Form S-3 (File No. 333-294504) that was previously filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) on March 20, 2026, and became automatically effective upon filing. The preliminary prospectus supplement and accompanying base prospectus relating to and describing the terms of the offering has been filed with the SEC, and a final prospectus supplement relating to and describing the terms of the offering will be filed with the SEC and will be available on the SEC’s website located at http://www.sec.gov. The offering is being made only by means of a prospectus and related prospectus supplement, copies of which may be obtained, when available, from J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, c/o Broadridge Financial Solutions, 1155 Long Island Avenue, Edgewood, NY 11717, or by email at prospectus-eq_fi@jpmorganchase.com and postsalemanualrequests@broadridge.com; or TD Securities (USA) LLC, Attention: Broadridge Financial Solutions, 1155 Long Island Avenue, Edgewood, NY 11717 or by email at TDManualrequest@broadridge.com.

This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell, or a solicitation of an offer to buy, nor will there be any sale of these securities in any state or other jurisdiction in which such an offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to the registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or other jurisdiction.

About SELLAS Life Sciences Group, Inc.

SELLAS is a late-stage clinical biopharmaceutical company focused on the development of novel therapeutics for a broad range of cancer indications. SELLAS’ lead product candidate, GPS, is licensed from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and targets the WT1 protein, which is present in an array of tumor types. GPS has the potential as a monotherapy and combination with other therapies to address a broad spectrum of hematologic malignancies and solid tumor indications. The Company is also developing SLS009 (tambiciclib), a small molecule CDK9 inhibitor, for the treatment of AML in patients with unfavorable prognostic factors including ASXL1 mutation, commonly associated with poor prognosis in various myeloid diseases.

IRVINE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--SBC Medical Group Holdings Incorporated (Nasdaq: SBC) ("SBC Medical Group" or the "Company"), a provider of comprehensive management services to medical corporations and their clinics, today reported the occurrence of recent cybersecurity incidents involving customer information associated with certain clinics in Japan, along with the status of its response.

Overview of the Incidents

On November 16, 2026, unauthorized access occurred to certain databases within a website system managed and operated by SBC Medical Group, Ltd., the Company’s, Japanese subsidiary, in connection with its management services in Japan. The Company confirmed that an unauthorized third party accessed and extracted customer information. The method of intrusion and full scope remain under investigation.

*Note: Information entered in the inquiry forms includes, in some cases, credit card information (14 individuals affected). The Company has confirmed that all of these credit cards were in a state in which additional payments could not be processed, such as having expired. The relevant period for entries in the inquiry forms is 2010–2018.

Customer passwords were also obtained. Employee account information, including names, IDs and passwords, was also obtained for employees of the Company’s group and the medical institutions it supports, involving approximately 20,000 records. For 459 employees, information provided at the time of employment, including bank account and pension-related information, withholding tax certificates and dependent exemption declarations, was also affected. Historical customer inquiries involving 14 individuals included credit card information. The categories and scope of affected information remain under investigation. As of the date of this release, the Company has not confirmed unauthorized acquisition of electronic medical records or information in the mySBC reservation site. Clinical care systems and direct treatment histories were outside the scope of the Company-managed database incident. The treatment-monitor information included image file names, not the images themselves.

Separately, on November 16, 2026, the Company was notified of unauthorized access to clinic administrator accounts on “Tribeau,” a third-party reservation service used by 56 clinics to which the Company provides management services. The platform operator identified the following accessed information :

The operator confirmed that the obtained information was not linked to case or review information, including photographs, on Tribeau. Email addresses, residential addresses, credit card information, passwords and electronic medical records were not included in that platform incident. The Company and the provider continue to investigate the access and its cause.

Response and Ongoing Investigation

After its security monitoring system detected anomalous activity on November 16, the Company took measures to isolate the affected server and block unauthorized access. It established an incident response team, preserved system logs, strengthened access restrictions and monitoring, and decided to commission a detailed investigation by external cybersecurity specialists.

Following notification from the Tribeau operator, all accounts of the clinics to which the Company provides management services on that platform had their passwords invalidated, and communications from the attacking sources were blocked. The Company continues to coordinate with the operator.

The Company reported the database incident to Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission on November 16. The Company will take appropriate and firm action, including consulting with the police. As of the date of this release, the Company has not confirmed any fraudulent use or other secondary misuse of personal information resulting from the incidents.

Potential Business Impact

The Company is continuing to assess the potential impact of the incidents on its business, financial condition and results of operations.

The SBC core segment’s revenue comprises franchising, procurement, management services, rental services and other revenue streams. Fees for certain services are determined by factors including clinic size, services utilized and operational characteristics, while procurement and certain management services revenue components vary with clinic activity. Rental services revenue relates principally to medical equipment leased to medical corporations. The extent to which the incidents may affect these revenue streams remains uncertain. The Company also expects to incur costs related to customer notification, call center operations, forensic investigation, legal and advisory services, compensation and other response measures, a portion of which may be covered by cyber insurance maintained by its Japanese subsidiary, subject to policy terms and limits.

The relevant medical corporations have decided to suspend television and certain other advertising for a limited period following the incidents, and the Company expects that new patient inquiries at the affected clinics may decline during that period. Compensation payments may also arise.

The Company is currently unable to reasonably estimate the financial or other impacts of the incidents. The Company’s assessment will continue as its investigation progresses.

SBC Medical is a Medical Services Organization providing management support across a wide range of healthcare fields, including advanced aesthetic healthcare, dermatology, orthopedics, fertility treatment, gynecology, dentistry, hair loss treatment (AGA), and ophthalmology. The Company manages a diverse portfolio of clinic brands and is expanding its global presence, particularly in the United States and Asia, through operations and medical tourism initiatives. The Company was listed on Nasdaq in September 2024 and was selected for inclusion in the Russell 3000® Index in June 2025.

DISTRIBUTED-WORKFORCE/OAKLAND, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Square Australia and National Australia Bank (NAB) are teaming up to make banking and payments simpler for Australian businesses and give them greater control over their cash flow.

For small businesses, including those in retail and hospitality, cash flow matters, margins matter and time matters. The partnership combines NAB’s business banking expertise with Square’s leading payments and business tools to make it easier for customers to manage the everyday work of running a business.

Initially, the partnership will provide eligible NAB customers using Square access to Square’s flexible transfer feature, giving them more control over when their available funds are sent to their NAB Business Transaction Account.

From February next year, businesses can set a close of day time for each day of the week, with Square initiating the transfer of their available funds to their NAB Business Transaction Account 15 minutes later.

NAB Group Executive Business and Private Banking Andrew Auerbach said the partnership reflected the bank’s ambition to keep supporting customers to make running their business easier.

“Many hospitality and retail businesses don’t operate nine to five,” Mr. Auerbach said.

“A restaurant might finish trading late at night and need to pay suppliers the next morning. A café might need to buy tomorrow’s produce, so their banking and payments need to work around how they do business.

“NAB already supports businesses of all shapes and sizes across Australia. We want to keep raising the bar by finding practical ways to make running them easier.

“These sound like small things, but they can make a big difference when you’re running a business. Flexible transfer is the first Square feature being made available through the partnership and we want to build on it.”

Block Global Partnerships Lead Morgan Kuntze said the partnership combined Square’s technology and understanding of sellers with NAB’s expertise in business banking.

“Square works with businesses every day, helping them take payments and manage the day-to-day work that sits behind making a sale,” Ms. Kuntze said.

“By partnering with NAB, we can connect that experience more closely with banking and find new ways to make managing money simpler for sellers.

“Flexible transfer is the first step. Sellers can set their close of day schedule around the way their business operates, and Square automatically initiates the transfer of their available funds.”

For Axil Coffee Roasters, which has grown from a single Hawthorn cafe to more than 16 locations and hundreds of wholesale partners, managing cash flow is part of the everyday reality of running a growing hospitality business.

“There’s no standard working day in hospitality,” said Axil Managing Director David Makin.

“Some of our venues open incredibly early, others trade later, and every day we’re managing staff, stock and suppliers across the business.

“Being able to set our transfer schedule around how we actually trade gives us another level of control over our cash flow.

“We need the flexibility. The more our banking and payments can fit around how the business actually operates, rather than the other way around, the better.”

Through the partnership, NAB and Square plan to build on flexible transfer by exploring further ways to connect banking and payments, simplify cash flow and make it easier for Australian businesses to operate and grow.

NAB has opened up the ability for businesses to express interest in the partnership ahead of the full launch in early 2027 - click here for more information.

Notes to editors:

  • NAB’s current standard settlement time is 9.30pm AEST daily.
  • Square’s flexible transfers require a linked and eligible NAB Business Transaction Account. The availability of funds in the linked bank account may be affected by NAB processing requirements.
  • Square applies transfer limits ranging from $5 to $50,000 AUD per day (new sellers are limited to $5,000 AUD per day until eligible for a higher limit). Flexible Transfers may not be available in limited circumstances beyond Square’s control, including where the linked bank account is not eligible for real-time payments or where there is downtime or delay affecting the New Payments Platform. Square’s Terms of Service apply.

About Square
Square helps businesses turn transactions into connections and businesses into neighbourhood favourites. In 2009, Square started with a simple invention — the first mobile card reader, which changed how the entire financial system thinks about small businesses. Square has since grown into a global business platform helping millions of sellers of all sizes participate and thrive in their communities. Whether independently run or a global chain, Square understands that sellers succeed when they have the freedom to focus on the experiences that keep customers coming back. From point of sale and payments to online commerce, staff management, cash flow tools, and more, Square brings together the tools sellers need to run and grow on one intelligent platform. For more information, visit squareup.com.

About NAB
At National Australia Bank (NAB) Group, our ambition is to be the most customer-centric company in Australia and New Zealand. More than 41,000 colleagues at the bank provide 10 million customers with secure, easy and reliable banking services. About 88% of the Group’s workforce are located in Australia and New Zealand, while others work in Asia, London, New York and Paris. NAB is proud to be Australia’s largest business lender. We stand by our customers, and they have our ongoing support.

DELTA, British Columbia, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- RecycLiCo Battery Materials Inc. (“RecycLiCo” or the “Company”) (TSX.V: AMY | OTCQB: AMYZF | FSE: ID4), a critical minerals refining and lithium-ion battery upcycling company, is pleased to announce the results of its 2026 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders, held November 17, 2026.

Shareholders representing approximately 31.82% of the Company’s issued and outstanding shares participated in person or by proxy and approved all matters of business before the meeting, including the setting of the number of directors, the election of directors, and the appointment of the auditor.

Richard Sadowsky (Interim CEO), Paul Hildebrand (Chairman), Rod Langtry, Kurt Lageschulte and Rob Chang were each re-elected to serve as directors of the Company until the next annual meeting of shareholders or until their successors are duly elected or appointed.

Richard Sadowsky, Interim CEO of RecycLiCo said, “On behalf of the entire Board and management team, I want to thank our shareholders for their participation and continued engagement. We appreciate the perspectives shared by shareholders at the meeting and remain committed to disciplined execution, responsible research and development, and creating sustainable long-term value as we work to support a secure and resilient domestic supply of critical minerals and metals for North America.”

The shareholders also approved the re-appointment of De Visser Gray LLP as the Company’s auditor until the close of the next annual meeting.

About RecycLiCo 

RecycLiCo Battery Materials Inc. is a critical minerals refining company specializing in the use of advanced hydrometallurgical technologies for processing mined ore and the upcycling of lithium-ion battery materials. RecycLiCo’s processes efficiently recover battery-ready lithium, cobalt, nickel, and manganese from end-of-life batteries and manufacturing scrap, supporting energy storage as well as broader industrial applications. RecycLiCo’s business focus aligns with the global demand for future-ready, responsible supply chains and the growing movement to strengthen domestic sourcing of critical materials.

Lenovo delivers record Q2 performance, confident in long-term Hybrid AI opportunities

HONG KONG--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY), together with its subsidiaries (‘the Group’), today reported second quarter results for fiscal year 2026/27, demonstrating strong growth, a leap forward in profitability, and structural enhancements to the Group’s business fundamentals.

Overall Group revenue for the second quarter reached an all-time high of US$30.2 billion, up 48% year-on-year. All business groups delivered record second-fiscal-quarter revenue while demonstrating strong profitability, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) becoming an engine of hyper-growth with operating profit surpassing US$1 billion for the first time. Adjusted net income[1] was up 166% year-on-year to US$1.4 billion, with adjusted net margin improvements of two percentage points year-on-year. AI-related revenue[2] grew 79% year-on-year, surpassing the US$10 billion mark for the first time and accounting for 36% of total Group revenue in Q2.

Performance was underpinned by broad-based momentum across the Group’s diversified portfolio and balanced growth across all sales geographies. Business fundamentals continued to strengthen as faster growth in higher-value segments reshaped the Group’s profit mix. This diversification helps mitigate industry-wide cost pressures and exposure to device-demand cycles, supporting a more resilient and sustainable profitability profile.

The Group continues to maintain disciplined cash and capital management, balancing strong revenue growth and industry-wide higher component costs with controlled capital expenditure and credit risk controls for large AI infrastructure projects. In this quarter, it generated US$1.6 billion in operating cash flow and US$1.2 billion in free cash flow.

Market Outlook

Lenovo remains highly confident in the long-term growth opportunities across both infrastructure and devices. As AI shifts from training to inferencing, rapidly expanding real-world use cases are driving sustained compute demand across cloud, edge, and enterprise environments. Cloud Service Provider revenue for the Group grew nearly 170% year-on-year, and Enterprise & SMB infrastructure revenue was up 200% year-on-year. At the same time, AI democratization is creating new demand for intelligent, agent-enabled devices as well as new form factors, as more AI data and workloads are generated at the edge. With a full-stack Hybrid AI portfolio spanning devices, edge, infrastructure, solutions and services, Lenovo is uniquely positioned as a full-stack player to capture opportunities and value across the market, as well as extend its leadership.

Lenovo’s Board of Directors declared an interim dividend of 9.0 HK cents per share.

Chairman and CEO quote – Yuanqing Yang:

“Lenovo delivered another exceptional quarter, where we have sustained strong growth, made a leap forward in profitability, and structurally enhanced our business fundamentals, together demonstrating the success of our transformation from a PC leader into a global full-stack compute leader. Now, the real-world AI adoption is booming, which will not only drive sustained growth in infrastructure demand but also unlock tremendous growth potential in the device market. With our Hybrid AI strategy, full-stack portfolio across Client-Edge-Cloud, as well as strong financial discipline and operational resilience, we are confident in sustaining this strong momentum and reaching US$100 billion in annual revenue as early as this fiscal year.”

CFO quote – Winston Cheng:

“Our results this quarter demonstrate the strength of Lenovo’s geographically diverse business and balanced customer mix, while marking further progress toward our long-term net-margin ambitions of more than 5%. This, combined with disciplined working-capital management and controlled capital expenditure, gives us the flexibility to invest in organic growth while maintaining strong liquidity, a resilient balance sheet and our investment-grade credit profile. Together, our operational excellence and financial discipline position Lenovo to capture long-term demand for AI compute and deliver sustainable, profitable growth.”

HAMBURG, Germany, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Evotec SE (NASDAQ: EVO) (Frankfurt Prime Standard: EVT) today announced that its strategic protein degradation partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb has received a second Investigational New Drug (IND) acceptance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The first candidate produced under the partnership entered a Phase 1 clinical trial in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma in March 2026. The second accepted investigational drug candidate, a cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD), is expected to enter a Phase 1 clinical trial in 2027.

Initiated in 2018, the partnership combines Evotec's high-performance multi-omics screening, AI-supported data analytics, and drug design capabilities with Bristol Myers Squibb's industry-leading CELMoD agent library. This collaboration, expanded in 2022, continues to advance a pipeline of novel molecular glue degraders for high-value targets in oncology and beyond, translating scientific innovation into a growing therapeutic pipeline.

Dr. Joanna Holbrook, Chief Scientific Officer of Evotec, commented:

"The progression of a second molecular glue candidate to IND acceptance demonstrates the repeatability and productivity of our discovery platform. We are systematically translating complex biology into development candidates. This achievement reinforces the value of our longstanding collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb and further strengthens our confidence in the platform's potential to generate a growing pipeline of investigational drug candidates aimed at addressing substantial unmet medical needs."

About molecular glue degraders

Conventional small molecule therapeutics act through drug-induced interference with protein activity. This limitation to agonistic or antagonistic functions renders about 90% of proteins 'undruggable'. Also, conventional small molecules only work while they are actively binding to the receptor, which typically requires a treatment regimen consisting of one or even several carefully dosed medications every day.

Molecular glue degraders are compounds that induce interactions between an E3 ubiquitin ligase and a molecular target. The induced interaction results in ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of the recruited protein. By inducing neomorphic interactions between CRBN and substrate proteins, CELMoDs enable pharmacological modulation of proteins that may not be amenable to traditional inhibitor or agonist approaches, thereby expanding the potentially druggable proteome.

About Evotec's strategic collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb in molecular glues

In 2018, Evotec entered a long-term strategic drug discovery and development collaboration in the field of molecular glues with Celgene, now Bristol Myers Squibb. Bristol Myers Squibb is a leader in this field based on its unique library of CELMoD agents. The collaboration aims to discover and develop a leading pipeline of molecular glue degraders for a range of therapeutic indications leveraging all of Evotec's proprietary PanOmics and PanHunter platforms as well as AI/ML-based drug discovery and development capabilities.

Evotec applies high-end proteomics and transcriptomics at industrial scale to profile and select promising drug candidates based on comprehensive cell biological profiles. Evotec's leading PanOmics screening capabilities are delivering unmatched throughput. The selection of the most promising candidates for drug development is facilitated by Evotec's PanOmics data analysis platform PanHunter. By integrating and analyzing these data sets, PanHunter supports the identification and advancement of the most promising CELMoDs into lead optimization.

About Evotec SE

Evotec is a life science company pioneering the future of drug discovery and development. By integrating breakthrough science with AI-driven innovation and advanced technologies, Evotec accelerates the journey from concept to cure with greater speed, intelligence and precision. The company's expertise spans small molecules, biologics, cell therapies and associated modalities, supported by proprietary platforms including Molecular Patient Databases, PanOmics and induced pluripotent stem cell-based disease modeling. Through flexible partnering models tailored to customers' needs, Evotec works with all Top 20 pharmaceutical companies, more than 800 biotechnology companies, academic institutions and other healthcare stakeholders. Evotec's offerings range from standalone services to fully integrated research and development programs and long-term strategic partnerships, combining scientific excellence with operational agility. Through Just - Evotec Biologics, the company is redefining biologics development and manufacturing to improve accessibility and affordability. With a portfolio of more than 100 proprietary research and development assets, most of which are co-owned, Evotec focuses on key therapeutic areas including oncology, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, neurology and immunology. Evotec's global team of around 4,500 experts operates from sites in Europe and the United States, providing complementary technologies and services through a network of synergistic centers of excellence. TORRANCE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Emmaus Life Sciences, Inc. (OTCQB: EMMA), a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company and leader in the treatment of sickle cell disease, today reported on its financial condition and results of operations as of and for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights

“Our global net revenues declined for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025 primarily driven by a 44% decrease in U.S. net revenues as our licensing agreement with NeoImmuneTech Inc. (NIT), became effective on May 15, 2026,” commented Willis Lee, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Emmaus. “The decline was partially offset by a related reduction in our operating expenses. Management believes that the conflict in the Middle East also adversely affected net revenues in the region,” he added.

Financial and Operating Results

Net Revenues. Net revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $1.9 million, compared to $3.4 million in the same period in 2025 driven by lower direct sales of Endari® following the company’s execution of the License Agreement with NIT.

Operating Expenses. Total operating expenses for the three months were $1.9 million compared to $2.4 million in the comparable period in 2025. The decrease was due primarily to decreased expenses attributable to the transfer of our sales force to NIT in connection with the license arrangement.

Income (Loss) From Operations. Loss from operations for the three months was $0.4 million compared to income from operations of $0.7 million in the same period in 2025. The changes were due to the decrease in net revenues, partially offset by lower operating expenses.

Other Expense. The company realized other expense of $4.4 million for the three months compared to $2.2 million in the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily due to change in fair value of conversion features derivative based upon an increase in the company’s stock price.

Net Loss. For the three months, the company realized a net loss of $4.7 million, or $0.07 basic loss per share based on approximately 70.2 million weighted-average common shares, compared to net loss of $2.1 million, or $0.03 basic loss per share based on approximately 63.9 million weighted-average common shares in the comparable period in 2025. The increase in net loss was attributable primarily to the decrease in net revenues and increase in other expense.

Liquidity and Capital Resources. At September 30, 2026, the company had cash and cash equivalents of $1.0 million, compared to $2.1 million at December 31, 2025.

About Emmaus Life Sciences

Emmaus Life Sciences, Inc. is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company and leader in the treatment of sickle cell disease. Endari® (L-glutamine oral powder), indicated to reduce the acute complications of sickle cell disease in adults and children 5 years and older, is approved for marketing in the United States, Israel, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Oman and is available on a named patient or early access basis in France, the Netherlands, and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where Emmaus’ application for marketing authorization is awaiting final action by the Saudi Food & Drug Authority. For more information, please visit www.emmausmedical.com.

About Endari® (prescription grade L-glutamine oral powder)

Endari®, Emmaus’ prescription grade L-glutamine oral powder, was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in July 2017 for treating sickle cell disease in adult and pediatric patients five years of age and older.

Indication

Endari® is indicated to reduce the acute complications of sickle cell disease in adult and pediatric patients five years of age and older.

Important Safety Information

The most common adverse reactions (incidence >10 percent) in clinical studies were constipation, nausea, headache, abdominal pain, cough, pain in extremities, back pain, and chest pain.

Adverse reactions leading to treatment discontinuation included one case each of hypersplenism, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, burning sensation, and hot flash.

The safety and efficacy of Endari® in pediatric patients with sickle cell disease younger than five years of age has not been established.

For more information, please see full Prescribing Information of Endari® at: www.ENDARIrx.com/PI.

About Sickle Cell Disease

There are approximately 100,000 people living with sickle cell disease (SCD) in the United States and millions more globally. The sickle gene is found in every ethnic group, not just among those of African descent; and in the United States an estimated 1-in-365 African Americans and 1-in-16,300 Hispanic Americans are born with SCD.1 The genetic mutation responsible for SCD causes an individual's red blood cells to distort into a "C" or a sickle shape, reducing their ability to transport oxygen throughout the body. These sickled red blood cells break down rapidly, become very sticky, and develop a propensity to clump together, which causes them to become stuck and cause damage within blood vessels. The result is reduced blood flow to distal organs, which leads to physical symptoms of incapacitating pain, tissue and organ damage, and early death.2

CLEVELAND, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyster‑Yale, Inc. (NYSE: HY) today announced the pricing of its offering of $135,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 7.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031 (the "notes") in a private offering to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"). The offering size was increased from the previously announced offering size of $125,000,000 aggregate principal amount of notes. The issuance and sale of the notes is scheduled to close on November 23, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Hyster‑Yale granted the initial purchasers of the notes an option to purchase, for settlement within a period of 13 days from, and including, the date the notes are first issued, up to an additional $20,000,000 aggregate principal amount of notes.

The notes will be general senior unsecured obligations of Hyster‑Yale and will accrue interest at a rate of 7.50% per annum, payable semi-annually in arrears on May 15 and November 15 of each year, beginning on May 15, 2027. The notes will mature on November 15, 2031, unless earlier repurchased, redeemed or converted in accordance with their terms. Before July 15, 2031, noteholders will have the right to convert their notes only upon the occurrence of certain events. At any time from, and including, July 15, 2031, noteholders may convert their notes at their election until the close of business on the second scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date, irrespective of these conditions. Hyster‑Yale will settle conversions by paying cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted and paying or delivering, as applicable, cash, shares of its Class A common stock (the "Class A common stock") or a combination of cash and shares of Class A common stock, at Hyster‑Yale's election, in respect of the remainder, if any, of its conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted. The initial conversion rate is 55.1207 shares of Class A common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes, which represents an initial conversion price of approximately $18.14 per share of Class A common stock. The initial conversion price represents a premium of approximately 17.5% over the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on November 18, 2026, which was $15.44 per share. The conversion rate will be subject to adjustment upon the occurrence of certain events, but will not be adjusted for any accrued and unpaid interest.

Hyster‑Yale may not redeem the notes prior to November 20, 2029, except in the event of a cleanup redemption (as defined below). The notes will be redeemable, in whole or in part (subject to certain limitations, including a partial redemption limitation), for cash at Hyster‑Yale's option at any time, and from time to time, on a redemption date on or after November 20, 2029 and before the 61st scheduled trading day immediately prior to the maturity date, if the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock has been at least 130% of the conversion price then in effect for a specified period of time and if certain other conditions are satisfied. The redemption price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the relevant redemption date.

In addition, Hyster‑Yale may redeem for cash all, but not less than all, of the notes at any time before the 61st scheduled trading day immediately prior to the maturity date if the aggregate principal amount of the notes that remains outstanding at such time is less than 10% of the aggregate principal amount of the notes initially issued under the indenture and certain other conditions are satisfied (a "cleanup redemption"). The redemption price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the relevant redemption date.

If certain corporate events that constitute a "fundamental change" (as defined in the indenture that will govern the notes) occur, then, subject to certain conditions and exceptions, noteholders may require Hyster‑Yale to repurchase their notes for cash. The fundamental change repurchase price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the applicable fundamental change repurchase date.

Hyster‑Yale estimates that the net proceeds from the offering will be approximately $129.7 million (or approximately $149.1 million if the initial purchasers fully exercise their option to purchase additional notes), after deducting the initial purchasers' discounts and commissions and Hyster‑Yale's estimated offering expenses. Hyster‑Yale intends to use the net proceeds from the offering of the notes, together with cash on hand, (i) to repay $110.0 million of the $213.2 million principal amount outstanding under the term loan under its Amended and Restated Term Loan Credit Agreement, dated as of May 28, 2021 (the "2021 Credit Agreement"), (ii) to pay the approximately $13.5 million cost of the capped call transactions (as described below), (iii) to repurchase approximately $15 million of shares of Class A common stock concurrently with the pricing of the notes (as described below), and (iv) for general corporate purposes. If the initial purchasers exercise their option to purchase additional notes, Hyster‑Yale expects to use a portion of the net proceeds from the sale of the additional notes to enter into additional capped call transactions with the option counterparties, to repay additional principal amounts outstanding under the term loan under its 2021 Credit Agreement and, to the extent any proceeds remain, for general corporate purposes. The Company intends to repay the remaining principal amount outstanding under the term loan under its 2021 Credit Agreement on or prior to its maturity with additional long-term debt that is on terms acceptable to the Company.

Hyster‑Yale expects to use approximately $15 million of the net proceeds from the offering to repurchase approximately 971,000 shares of Class A common stock in privately negotiated transactions effected with or through one of the initial purchasers or its affiliate concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the notes (the "concurrent share repurchase"). The purchase price per share in the concurrent share repurchase will be $15.44 per share, which is the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on the date of the pricing of the notes. The concurrent share repurchase could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of Class A common stock, including concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the notes, and could have resulted in a higher effective conversion price for the notes. Hyster‑Yale cannot predict the magnitude of such market activity or the overall effect it will have on the price of the notes or the Class A common stock and the corresponding effect on the initial conversion price of the notes.

In connection with the pricing of the notes, Hyster‑Yale entered into privately negotiated capped call transactions with certain of the initial purchasers and their affiliates and certain other financial institutions (the "option counterparties"). The capped call transactions cover, subject to customary adjustments substantially similar to those applicable to the notes, the number of shares of Class A common stock initially underlying the notes. The capped call transactions are generally expected to reduce the potential dilution to the Class A common stock upon any conversion of the notes and/or offset any potential cash payments Hyster‑Yale is required to make in excess of the principal amount of such converted notes, as the case may be, with such reduction and/or offset subject to a cap based on the cap price. The cap price of the capped call transactions is initially $27.02 per share, which represents a premium of 75% over the last reported sale price per share of the Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on November 18, 2026 (which was $15.44 per share), and is subject to certain adjustments under the terms of the capped call transactions. If the initial purchasers exercise their option to purchase additional notes, then Hyster‑Yale expects to enter into additional capped call transactions with the option counterparties.

Hyster‑Yale has been advised that, in connection with establishing their initial hedges of the capped call transactions, the option counterparties or their respective affiliates expect to enter into various derivative transactions with respect to the Class A common stock and/or purchase shares of Class A common stock concurrently with, or shortly after, the pricing of the notes. This activity could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of the Class A common stock or the notes at that time.

In addition, Hyster-Yale has been advised that the option counterparties or their respective affiliates may modify their hedge positions by entering into or unwinding various derivatives with respect to the Class A common stock and/or purchasing or selling the Class A common stock or other securities of Hyster‑Yale in secondary market transactions following the pricing of the notes and prior to the maturity of the notes (and are likely to do so during any observation period related to a conversion of the notes, following any redemption of the notes or any repurchase of the notes upon a fundamental change, or, to the extent Hyster‑Yale exercises the relevant election under the capped call transactions, following any other repurchase of the notes). This activity could also cause or avoid an increase or a decrease in the market price of the Class A common stock or the notes, which could affect the ability of noteholders to convert the notes and, to the extent the activity occurs during any observation period related to a conversion of the notes, it could affect the number of shares of Class A common stock, if any, and value of the consideration that noteholders will receive upon conversion of the notes.

The notes are being offered only to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act. SAN ANTONIO, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As facility management continues to evolve from a largely operational function into a strategic contributor to workplace performance and enterprise resilience, JLL is demonstrating how an integrated approach can create measurable value for organizations across complex environments. Frost & Sullivan recognizes JLL with the 2026 North American Competitive Strategy Leadership Recognition in Facility Management for its ability to combine strategic transformation, digital capabilities, and sector expertise to strengthen its competitive position and deliver integrated facility management (IFM) solutions across the region.

Frost & Sullivan evaluates companies through a rigorous benchmarking process across two core dimensions: strategy effectiveness and strategy execution. JLL excelled in both, demonstrating its ability to align strategic initiatives with evolving market demands while executing them with consistency, scale, and measurable impact. "JLL is a recognized leader in IFM and workplace solutions across North America. Its competitive position is built on a clear strategic progression: redefining Facility Management through the Workplace Management platform, aligning its operating structure to support integrated delivery, and scaling digital and sector-specific capabilities across the United States and Canada. This approach enables JLL to serve commercial office, financial services, life sciences, technology, industrial and advanced manufacturing, data centers, healthcare, and government clients while linking facility operations more directly to business performance," said Janice Wung, Industry Principal, Homes & Buildings, Frost & Sullivan.

JLL's strategic approach centers on its Workplace Management platform, which brings together facilities management, technical services, sustainable operations, safety, sourcing and procurement, workplace experience, and technology-enabled delivery under a single operating structure. The platform supports greater standardization, governance, and scalability across multi-site portfolios while maintaining flexibility for sector-specific requirements.

Digital innovation further differentiates JLL's approach to facility management. Technologies, including Corrigo, JLL Smart Building Platform, Azara, and JLL Falcon AI, support work order and asset management, predictive maintenance, energy optimization, workplace analytics, and portfolio-level performance visibility. These capabilities enable clients to move beyond reactive facility operations toward more proactive, data-driven decision-making.

"We are honored Frost & Sullivan is recognizing JLL's work in facilities management," said Chris Fernandez, Americas Head of Workplace Management at JLL. "At its core, facilities management is about creating environments where people can do their best work while ensuring the buildings they depend on operate safely, reliably and efficiently every day. FM has evolved far beyond maintaining physical assets. Today, it sits at the intersection of workplace experience, operational resilience and business performance. This award reflects the dedication of our teams across North America who help clients care for both their buildings and the people inside them, ensuring workplaces support productivity, collaboration and long-term success."

Frost & Sullivan's recognition comes while broader changes are underway across the facility management industry. JLL's recent Global State of Facilities Management Report 2026 reveals that half of occupiers already view FM as a significant source of competitive advantage, with that figure projected to rise to more than four in five organizations by 2030. Meanwhile, 45% of occupiers are scaling AI across FM operations while nearly 70% have experienced disruptions from skilled labor shortages and technical skills gaps. These converging trends are accelerating demand for integrated workplace management strategies that combine operational expertise, technology and workforce capabilities to support business performance and resilience.

JLL has also demonstrated its ability to translate strategy into execution across complex, high-value environments. In 2025, the company secured integrated facilities management for WestJet's 1.9 million-square-foot portfolio spanning its headquarters and 17 Canadian airport locations, along with the facility maintenance and operations mandate for the $9.5 billion JFK New Terminal One project. For a global tech manufacturer, JLL moved the company's U.S. portfolio from reactive repairs to proactive IFM, saving nearly $1 million on HVAC costs in its first eight months and achieving 4% overall savings in the first year. JLL has also partnered with a Fortune 100 semiconductor company to build a digital FM strategy aimed at cost savings and operational excellence. Together, these engagements show JLL's ability to scale integrated facility management across demanding environments where reliability, compliance, operational resilience, and risk management are critical.

The company's competitive position is further strengthened by integrating energy management, decarbonization initiatives, ESG reporting, workplace experience, and space-utilization analysis into its FM delivery model, JLL addresses the increasingly interconnected priorities of corporate real estate, sustainability, HR, and business leaders.

Frost & Sullivan commends JLL for establishing a differentiated approach to facility management that connects operational performance with broader business outcomes. Through its combination of proprietary technology, advisory-led delivery, sector expertise, and customer-focused execution, JLL is helping shape the future of FM across North America.

Each year, Frost & Sullivan presents the Competitive Strategy Leadership recognition to a company that demonstrates outstanding strategy development and implementation, resulting in measurable improvements in market share, customer satisfaction, and competitive positioning. LAUREL, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--InTest Corporation (NYSE American: INTT), a global supplier of innovative test and process technology solutions, today announced the launch of the BT-28 ECO, a next-generation benchtop air forcing system from InTest Thermal Solutions. Designed to meet and exceed the requirements of European Union Regulation (EU) 2024/573, the BT-28 ECO advances precision thermal testing while helping customers respond to a rapidly changing refrigerant and sustainability landscape.

“We designed the BT-28 ECO to meet emerging European F-gas requirements without asking customers to give up speed, accuracy, workspace or ease of use. It is a strong example of our commitment to helping customers boost performance while preparing their operations for a more sustainable future,” said Scott Taylor, Vice President and General Manager of InTest’s Environmental Technologies division.

“The BT-28 ECO shows how InTest’s leadership and focus on innovation in precision temperature control translate into value-creating solutions for our customers,” added Rich Rogoff, President and Chief Executive Officer of InTest Corporation.

The BT-28 ECO delivers a temperature range of -28°C to +225°C utilizing refrigerants with a GWP less than 5.0. It transitions from -10°C to +125°C, and back, in approximately 10 seconds or less, while providing 14 scfm (6.5 l/s) airflow across the full temperature range. The system delivers temperature resolution of ±0.1°C and temperature accuracy of 1.0°C when calibrated against a NIST standard.

Engineered for laboratories and production environments where floor and bench space are at a premium, the portable system measures approximately 13.9 inches wide by 23.4 inches deep by 16.7 inches high and weighs approximately 80 pounds. Its ECO-Stream design is smaller, quieter and more energy-efficient, with operating sound levels below 60 dBA and below 50 dBA at idle.

Regulatory readiness
Designed to meet and exceed EU 2024/573 requirements and support the transition to lower-GWP refrigerants.

Industry-leading benchtop performance
Fast transitions, 14 scfm airflow and a -28°C to +225°C operating range.

Compact, quiet operation
Portable benchtop footprint with <60 dBA operation and <50 dBA at idle.

Flexible control
Detachable touchscreen with a 9-foot (3-meter) remote cable and proprietary direct DUT temperature control.

Serviceability and safety
Auto-diagnostics, field-replaceable modules and operator-set high and low temperature limits.

 

The detachable touchscreen can be positioned within the reach of the supplied remote cable, giving operators greater flexibility around the test area. Available accessories include thermal caps, bench clamps, a control cradle, tall and short carts, custom enclosures and non-conductive mats.

The Agreement represents a further step in First Graphene's strategy to commercialise its graphene technologies through strategic development and manufacturing partnerships. The collaboration will combine First Graphene's expertise in graphene selection, formulation and dispersion with UNITEX's materials engineering, manufacturing infrastructure and established supply chain capabilities.

UNITEX brings extensive expertise in materials development, engineering and manufacturing, alongside an established international customer network. This collaboration provides FGR with a strategic pathway into China's composites manufacturing sector and expand its commercial reach across global markets.

Importantly, the opportunity extends well beyond carbon fibre. By combining our respective technical and manufacturing capabilities, we see significant potential to develop graphene-enhanced thermoplastics, coatings and other advanced materials across industrial applications.

This agreement is another important step in our strategy to move graphene innovation from development into commercial markets and expand First Graphene's international presence."

  • Net cash as of September 30, 2026 was US$2940.5 million.
  • Net cash from operating activities was US$102.2 million.

Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights

Social Entertainment Business

In the third quarter, Social Entertainment continued to deliver steady growth, with year-over-year growth momentum further accelerating. The Company's global average mobile MAUs reached 278.8 million, up 4.7% year over year. Livestreaming revenue reached US$419.8 million, up 8.1% year over year and 4.3% quarter over quarter. Driven by effective and refined operations, the number of core livestreaming paying users grew 8.1% year over year and 4.8% quarter over quarter.

Bigo Live, the Company's flagship product, continued its steady revenue growth, supported by ongoing improvements in content operations, its streamer ecosystem, and AI applications. In content operations, Bigo Live continued to build on its strengths as a global social platform to better cater to users' cross-regional content consumption and social interaction needs. Bigo Live further refined its cross-regional content distribution algorithms, expanded live translation coverage, and enhanced speech recognition in complex acoustic environments, making it easier for cross-language communication. These improvements drove continued growth in cross-regional gifting among users in developed markets. In terms of the streamer ecosystem, Bigo Live continued to invest in its community by refining growth and incentive mechanisms for new streamers. In particular, Bigo Live improved onboarding and guidance to help newly signed streamers successfully launch their first livestreams. These efforts contributed to a 4.7-percentage-point increase in the share of newly signed streamers completing their first livestream compared with the previous quarter, bolstering Bigo Live's high-quality content pipeline. Bigo Live continued to integrate AI into livestream interactions and virtual gifting, expanding its AI-generated interactive content and virtual gifts to create a more personalized experience for users. In September, the share of total virtual gift consumption attributable to AI-generated interactive virtual gifts increased further to 35.4%.

Furthermore, Bigo Live continued to deepen local community engagement and foster vibrant creator ecosystems. In the Middle East and North Africa, as an official content partner of the 2026 Esports World Cup, Bigo Live delivered an immersive viewing format that integrated tournament livestreams with interactive experiences. Across Southeast Asia, Bigo Live hosted multiple mid-year galas in local markets, supporting the growth of local creators and the sustainable development of its ecosystem. In North America, BIGO Academy combined online growth challenges with offline recognition, highlighting the vitality of its creator ecosystem and strong user engagement. In South America, Bigo Live held its inaugural offline event in Brazil and organized roadshows in Colombia and Peru, expanding public awareness of the platform and fostering a more vibrant and inclusive local creator ecosystem.

BIGO Ads Advertising Technology Business

In the third quarter, BIGO Ads continued to expand its global traffic network, diversify its advertiser verticals and demand mix, while improving its algorithms and ad delivery efficiency. As a result, BIGO Ads' revenue reached US$145.7 million, up 39.6% year over year and 9.0% quarter over quarter. Its third-party advertising business, BIGO Audience Network, grew 52.3% year over year and 9.2% quarter over quarter.

On the supply side, BIGO Ads continued to expand its global developer ecosystem and broaden the high-quality traffic coverage. In the third quarter, SDK traffic grew 55.6% year over year. This integration creates new opportunities for BIGO Ads to expand its premium traffic supply and reach a broader range of app categories.

On the demand side, BIGO Ads continued to strengthen its presence in key verticals by expanding its local advertiser base and accumulating more advertiser conversion data. These insights helped further refine its algorithms and optimize ad delivery solutions across different web-based verticals. Web-based advertising demand continued to accelerate, growing by approximately 328% year over year and 30% quarter over quarter, becoming a key driver of BIGO Ads' growth this quarter. Meanwhile, in-app demand maintained healthy growth momentum.

On the technology side, BIGO Ads continued to enhance its data and AI-driven algorithm capabilities to improve the precision and efficiency of ad delivery. As its cross-channel attribution systems improved and advertiser conversion data accumulated, the platform further upgraded its model architecture to support multiple conversion objectives and types of traffic, improving algorithm accuracy and iteration efficiency. Meanwhile, BIGO Ads continued to refine its bidding strategies to better assess the value of each ad impression and match advertiser budgets with available inventory more effectively. These improvements helped advertisers meet their ROI targets while enhancing the efficiency of BIGO Ads' traffic acquisition and monetization.

In AI Commerce, SHOPLINE's strategy revolves around helping merchants capture demand from AI channels and improve their operational efficiency. As AI agents change how consumers discover and purchase products, SHOPLINE continued to strengthen its capabilities and expand integrations with the broader AI ecosystem. While volume from AI channels is still in an early stage, adoption is building quickly. SHOPLINE Omi, an AI-powered commerce assistant, has rolled out features spanning product management, customer segmentation, promotional events, guidance on platform features and settings, and detailed store performance analysis, bringing AI deeper into merchants' day-to-day workflows and improving operational efficiency.

floating-ratefinancial

TORONTO, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Talisker Resources Ltd. ("Talisker" or the "Company") (TSX: TSK, OTCQX: TSKFF) is pleased to provide an update on the continued advancement of its ore sorter facility (“Sorting Facility”) at the Company’s 100% owned Bralorne Gold Project (“Bralorne”).   Construction and engineering activities have continued to advance according to plan, with several major project milestones already completed and a number of critical work programs now entering the execution phase.

Key Highlights:

  • Initial operation of the Sorting Facility is targeted for Q2 2027, with full commissioning expected in July-August 2027.
  • Electrical infrastructure is completed and targeted for commissioning by the end of November 2026, providing power for the future operation of the Sorting Facility.
  • Phase 1 earthworks associated with the electrical infrastructure required to support the Sorting Facility were successfully completed in September.
  • Phase 2 earthworks and concrete foundation construction is planned to commence late November 2026, following removal of legacy infrastructure.
  • Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) of the TOMRA XRT Sorter is scheduled for early December 2026, with the ore sorter expected to arrive in Canada in January 2027.
  • Major long-lead equipment procurement is substantially complete, with the jaw crusher, cone crusher, vibrating screen plant received in Bralorne in October, conveyors, compressors, and buildings being delivered in phases starting December 2026.
  • Construction and mechanical installation activities are planned throughout Q1 2027, supported by completion of detailed engineering and issuance of the remaining construction tender packages in December 2026.

Phase 1 earthworks associated with the electrical infrastructure required to support the Sorter Facility was successfully completed in September. The electrical infrastructure has been procured and installed, with final commissioning scheduled for the end of November 2026. The Mustang Mine power generation and distribution system consists of two 1.5 MW diesel generators, providing a total installed generation capacity of 3 MW at 600 V. The generators can operate in parallel or independently, providing redundancy and backup capability.

Power for the underground mining operations is stepped up to 4.16 kV through a 3,200 kVA transformer and distributed to underground substations that will supply mining equipment.

Surface power distribution is installed and ready to serve the sorting and crushing facilities, as well as supporting all other surface infrastructure requirements. The electrical system incorporates protective switchgear, circuit breakers, ground-fault monitoring, and neutral grounding resistors to ensure safe and reliable operation during the next phase of project development. The power plant and distribution network have also been designed to accommodate the future addition of a third generator unit, allowing for straightforward expansion of site power capacity as operational requirements increase.

As part of the ore sorter site preparation activities, a legacy electrical system located within the planned Sorting Facility footprint has been safely dismantled and removed, clearing part of the area for Phase 2 Earthworks construction. In parallel, the Company has completed construction of a new tension-fabric steel frame heavy-duty mechanic shop and is currently transitioning operations from the legacy shop. Demolition of the former shop is expected to be completed in November, fully opening the sorter site for Phase 2 Earthworks before the end of November.

The Phase 2 Earthworks and concrete contractor is scheduled to mobilize to site in November, marking the beginning of a major construction phase. This work will include cut-and-fill activities, foundation preparation, and pre-cast concrete installation within the area previously occupied by the legacy electrical infrastructure and mechanic shop.

Detailed engineering for the project continues to progress well. Issue-for-Tender packages covering the remaining construction components including equipment installation, electrical and mechanical are expected to be completed in December 2026, positioning the project for construction execution through the first half of 2027.

Procurement efforts have been highly successful, with all major equipment purchased. Equipment is either in manufacturing or pending delivery. A proactive approach to early procurement has significantly de-risked the project schedule and supports the Company's objective of maintaining construction momentum throughout the coming months.

A key milestone will occur during the second week of December when the Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) is conducted for the TOMRA XRT sorter. Following successful testing, the ore sorter is expected to arrive in Canada in January 2027.

The crushing circuit has also reached an important milestone, with all major crushing equipment including the jaw crusher, cone crusher, and vibrating screen plant, now delivered and in Bralorne. The compressor system required to support sorter operations is expected to ship for delivery in January 2027.

Building fabrication remains on track, with the manufacturing of two tension-fabric steel frame buildings completed and ready for shipment. The remaining two buildings are expected to be completed and shipped in January 2027.

Engineering and fabrication of the conveyor systems is progressing well. Initial conveyor deliveries are expected to begin arriving on site in mid-December, with additional conveyors being manufactured and shipped in priority sequence throughout the first quarter of 2027.

Taken together, these achievements represent substantial progress toward delivery of one of the Company's most important infrastructure projects. The project continues to transition from planning into full-scale execution with detailed engineering, procurement, and construction activities advancing simultaneously.

The Sorting Facility remains on schedule for operational readiness in the second quarter of 2027, with full commissioning anticipated during July-August 2027. Pre-commissioning activities will involve sorting existing stockpile inventory, providing an opportunity to validate system performance ahead of full scale operations. Once operational, the Sorting Facility will process run-of-mine material and is expected to enhance gold grades while eliminating dilution prior to trucking and shipping, improve operating efficiencies, reduce transportation costs, and strengthen project economics.

Terry Harbort, President and CEO, stated, "We are very pleased with the progress being made on the Sorting Facility. With key infrastructure completed, major equipment secured, and construction activities continuing to ramp up, the project remains on schedule for operational readiness in Q2 2027. This Sorting Facility represents an important milestone for Bralorne and will play a significant role in improving operational efficiency and supporting the Company's long-term growth objectives."


Figure 1: Aerial view of the Mustang Mine site with a rendered overlay of the sorting facility. The recently completed machine shop and the Mustang Mine power generation systems are shown to scale in their actual locations. The Sorting Facility rendering is provided for conceptual illustration only and may not be to scale. The product sorting process flow is indicated by the gold arrows, with major sorting equipment labelled in sequence from 1 through 4.


Figure 2: 3D rendering of the Sorting Facility. The product sorting process flow is indicated by the gold arrows, with major sorting equipment labelled in sequence. Run-of-mine material is loaded into the jaw crusher (1) via the loading ramp and conveyed to the triple-deck screening plant (2). Screened material is then transported to the TOMRA XRT sorter (3), where gold-bearing material is separated from waste rock. The sorted product is conveyed to the cone crusher (4) before being stockpiled within a covered tension-fabric storage building. Waste reject material is conveyed to a separate waste stockpile.
